page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6r.8xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated ARM64 vCPUs powered by an Ampere Altra processor clocked at 2.8 GHz. The server contains 64.0 GB of system memory, providing an allocation of 2.0 GB of RAM per virtual CPU core. It operates without bundled local SSD storage or GPU accelerators, relying on external network-attached block storage, and offers a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations highlight performance characteristics inherent to its multi-core ARM architecture. In single-threaded operations, such as single-core stress-ng tests, single-threaded gzip compression, single-threaded bzip3 decompression, and single-core Geekbench tasks, the instance scores within the bottom 25th percentile. Conversely, highly parallelized workloads leverage the 32 dedicated cores effectively, achieving performance in the top 25th percentile for multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Multi-core stress-ng tests, Geekbench multi-core scores, software compilation with Clang, Redis SET operations, static web serving, and small-model LLM inference rank within the middle 50th percentile.

The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM allocation provides dedicated core density for parallel processing while maintaining a lower memory footprint per core. The absence of local disk drives requires provisioning persistent network storage for operational files. The instance is suited for multi-threaded data decompression, CI/CD compilation jobs, containerized microservices, static web serving, and parallel execution tasks.

Performance benchmarks demonstrate weak single-core execution, with single-threaded gzip compression, bzip3 decompression, and single-core Geekbench scores landing in the bottom quartile. However, the architecture scales effectively across parallel execution threads, achieving top-tier performance in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression alongside middle-tier throughput in multi-core stress testing, software compilation, Redis operations, and static web serving. The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM balance delivers compute density tailored for multi-threaded workloads, distributed web applications, CI/CD compilation pipelines, and parallel data processing jobs relying on network-attached storage.
